q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to an 8-month-old for fever — it is not to be used in children younger than 6 months, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and know your child's weight before giving it [6]. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is another option, given every 4 to 6 hours [6].

The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the temperature itself down, according to the SEUP [5]. Make sure they are drinking well, keep the room at a neutral temperature, and avoid over-bundling them [5]. It is normal for them to have less appetite — do not force food, but keep offering plenty of fluids [5]. Do not bathe them in cold water or put wet cloths on them; it is unpleasant and does not work [5].

Get medical advice if you are worried about your child, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the main thing is to keep him drinking so he does not get dehydrated. Oral rehydration solution is the best choice for a child — you can buy it without a prescription [1]. Give small sips of rehydration solution often to replace lost fluids [5].

Do not give young children fruit juice or fizzy drinks, as these can make vomiting worse [5]. If he is on formula or solid foods, you can also give small sips of extra water [5].

If you are worried he is becoming dehydrated, speak to a pharmacist or your doctor [6]. Signs of dehydration include dark, smelly pee or peeing less than usual [6]. Severe dehydration may need treatment with fluids through a vein in hospital [1].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the common causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour. Watch how well they take it; if they keep it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids you can buy over the counter are the most helpful for mild dehydration; sports drinks without caffeine or alcohol can help a little, but they may not replace the important nutrients and minerals [2].

Get help if your child is very drowsy or limp, vomits many times, or will not take fluids [3]. If you think your child is severely dehydrated, call your doctor — severe dehydration may need fluids through a vein in hospital [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in children with asthma, and it can also be the first sign of a cold-like illness such as croup or whooping cough [4][5][3].

For asthma, the main symptoms are wheezing, coughing, shortness of breath and chest tightness, and they are often worse at night and early in the morning [4]. Croup causes a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing, and it is often worse at night [5]. Whooping cough starts like a cold, then brings coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night [3].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if asthma treatment is not helping or they are waking at night [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you think your child may have croup, or if they are getting worse or not getting better [5]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [6].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last for 10 to 14 days [6]. Croup also usually begins with cold-like symptoms — a temperature, runny nose and cough — and the cough may come on after a few days and be worse at night [3].

Keep offering fluids and let your son rest. There is no medicine in these sources for a lingering cough after a cold.

Ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor if you think your child may have croup, so the doctor can give medicine to shorten the illness, or if your child is getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [3]. Occasionally a child may be referred to hospital if they are more seriously ill or are under the age of 3 months [3].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually the body's response to a common infection like a cough or cold, according to the NHS [1]. Keep offering fluids and normal meals; a poor appetite for a few days is not harmful [2].

There is no fever here, so fever medicines are not needed. If a fever does appear, the AEPap says you can give paracetamol when the temperature is above 38–38.5°C (101.3 °F) in the armpit or when the fever is causing discomfort, every 4–6 hours, no more than five doses a day; the dose is calculated by weight [6]. Ibuprofen is an alternative, every 6–8 hours, but not if there is continued vomiting, and not under 3 months or under 5 kg [6].

Get help if he is under 3 months and has a temperature of 38°C (100.4 °F) or higher, is 3–6 months and has 39°C (102.2 °F) or higher, has a rash along with a high temperature, has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more, does not want to eat or is not his usual self, or is dehydrated [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear today could be many things, and the most useful thing is to look at what the spots are like. Raised, itchy patches or spots could be hives, which can usually be treated at home [5]. Chickenpox spots can be anywhere on the body, red or pink, and some become raised with a blister in the centre [4].

If it is chickenpox, keep your child off school or nursery until all the spots have scabbed over, usually 5 days after they first appeared [1]. Give plenty of fluids, paracetamol for pain or discomfort, and cut their fingernails and put socks on their hands at night to stop scratching [1]. Cooling creams or gels from a pharmacy can help, and a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine medicine for itching [1]. Bathe in cool water and pat the skin dry, and dress them in loose clothes [1]. Do not use ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections, and do not give aspirin to children under 16 [1].

Call your local emergency number if there is swelling around your child's mouth or they are struggling to breathe [5].

The main symptom of hives is an itchy rash of raised bumps or patches in many shapes and sizes, which can appear anywhere on the body and feel itchy, sting or burn [5]. Hives rashes usually get better within a few days, and you can often treat hives yourself [6].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [2][6]. The usual symptoms after a knock to the head are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

What to do now: watch him over the first 24 hours for any sign that things are getting worse [3]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor has indicated [6]. Keep him resting, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens during that time — then return to normal activities gradually [4].

Get urgent medical help if he has been knocked out and has not woken up, cannot stay awake or keep his eyes open, has a fit, has problems with his vision or hearing, has clear fluid coming from his ears or nose, is bleeding from his ears or has bruising behind his ears, has new numbness or weakness, has problems walking, with balance, understanding, speaking or writing, has a head wound with something inside it or a dent in his head, or his behaviour has changed, like being more irritable or distracted [2]. Get help also if he is being sick, feels dizzy, or has any other symptom that worries you [2]. From the SEUP: go to the emergency department if he has any of the symptoms above, or a behaviour or mood that worries you, or if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [2]. At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating — they'll still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

Start with small amounts, just a few pieces or teaspoons of food, offered before their usual milk feed when they're not too tired or too hungry [5]. Keep offering different foods, even ones they've rejected — it can take 10 tries or more before a baby accepts a new food or texture [5]. Offer a variety of foods, including fruit and vegetables, starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice, and protein such as beans, pulses, fish, eggs and meat [1]. Try to include iron-containing foods like meat, fish, fortified cereals, dark green vegetables, beans and lentils [1]. Don't add salt or sugar to their food or cooking water [1].

Move on from purées to mashed, lumpy or finger foods as soon as your baby can manage them [6]. Introduce a cup from around 6 months and offer sips of water with meals [5].

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text:
It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and fruit is part of a healthy diet — but vegetables matter too, so keep offering them. Your baby's diet should include a variety of fruit and vegetables, including ones with bitter flavours such as broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage, according to the NHS [1]. Vegetables help improve intake of some nutrients, especially iron, in babies 6 to 8 months old, and in all age groups from 6 to 23 months, according to the WHO [6].

Keep offering vegetables alongside fruit at meals, and offer them repeatedly — a baby may need to try a food many times before accepting it. The CDC has tips to help picky eaters try new foods [4]. Aim for 3 meals a day plus their usual milk feeds, and include iron-containing foods such as meat, fish, fortified cereals, dark green vegetables, beans and lentils [1].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula is no longer needed: your child can drink pasteurised whole or semi-skimmed cows' milk as their main drink, according to the NHS [2][4]. They should be eating 3 meals a day with a variety of foods — starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; milk or dairy products; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, dhal, beans, chickpeas or lentils — plus 2 healthy snacks between meals [2]. Full-fat dairy such as cheese, yoghurt and fromage frais is best, because children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in them [2]. Keep offering a variety alongside the milk; how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating [1]. If you use a milk alternative such as soya, oat or almond drink, choose one that is unsweetened and calcium-fortified [2]. Do not give rice drinks before 5 years old, because of the arsenic levels in them [2].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
For a newborn, the number of poops varies a lot from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby poops every day [3]. What matters more is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, sometimes with fewer poops than usual [6].

If you are worried, the SEUP says constipation in children should be managed by your paediatrician, and to go to the emergency department if there is: bad tummy pain, or the baby is very down and complaining a lot; blood in the stools; or repeated vomiting and not keeping down solids or liquids [3]. For a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding — breast milk or formula [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
For some babies aged 6 months to a year, night feeds may no longer be necessary, and teething discomfort or hunger may wake them during the night, according to the NHS [1]. Some babies this age may sleep for 5 to 8 hours or longer at night, but not all [3].

If your baby seems hungry, a breastfed baby will want to feed about every 2 hours, and a formula-fed baby should be able to go about 3 hours between feeds; during periods of rapid growth they may feed more often [2]. Being too hot or too cold can also disturb their sleep [3]. You do not need to give water to a baby — in fact, it could be dangerous [2]. An infant who is drinking enough will produce 6 to 8 wet diapers in a 24-hour period [2].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on mainly when he lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often causes coughing at night or early in the morning, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Asthma is a long-term lung condition where the airways become inflamed and narrowed, causing coughing, wheezing and chest tightness [4]. The NHS says asthma symptoms usually come and go and are often worse at night and early in the morning [5].

Keep the air moist — a steamy shower or vaporizer can help ease a cough, and water helps too [1]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four; for children over four, use caution and read labels carefully [1].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking him up at night [5]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [3].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual is a sign the asthma is not well controlled, and it is a reason to see your doctor [2]. Asthma cannot be cured, but with the right treatment most people can keep symptoms under control and live normally [1][2].

Keep using the inhaler as your child's plan says, and make sure it is used correctly — a spacer makes it easier and helps the medicine reach the lungs [1]. A doctor, nurse or pharmacist can show you how to use it properly [3].

See your doctor if your child needs the inhaler more often, if treatment is not helping, or if symptoms are stopping usual activities or waking them at night [2]. If an attack happens: sit your child up straight, stay calm, and give 1 puff of the reliever inhaler every 30 to 60 seconds, up to 10 puffs, shaking it between puffs and using a spacer if you have one [4]. Get emergency help if they get worse at any time, do not improve after the maximum dose, or have no inhaler [4]. After an attack, even if they feel better, see a doctor within 2 days [4].

Fast breathing that settles with rest is what the SEUP lists as a sign to watch for at home: difficulty breathing shows as ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, fast breathing, or getting tired when walking or running [3]. Because the warning above your text is already about fast breathing, follow what the sources say to do now and on the way to care.

The SEUP says to go to the emergency department when there is difficulty breathing, a poor general state, drowsiness, or being very irritable [3]. q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which often starts like a cold and then causes hoarseness, a barking cough and high-pitched sounds when breathing, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Most viral croup is mild and can be treated at home [3].

Keep her calm and comfortable, and let her rest; croup symptoms often get worse at night and usually last three to five days [3].

Get help if you are worried about her breathing — call your doctor straight away [3]. Also watch for difficulty breathing, such as the ribs pulling in, the chest sinking, fast breathing, or tiredness when walking or running, and for her becoming limp, sleepy or very irritable; these are reasons to go to the emergency department [1].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can be a sign of asthma, according to the WHO: asthma symptoms include chest tightness that makes it difficult to breathe deeply, and symptoms are often worse at night or during exercise [1]. The WHO also says symptoms can be caused by other conditions, and that people with symptoms should talk to a healthcare provider [1].

If your child has a cold, the SEUP says to watch at home for difficulty breathing — ribs showing or the chest sinking in, fast breathing, tiring when walking or running — or chest pain when breathing [2]. The SEUP says to go to the emergency department if your child's general condition gets worse, if they are listless, drowsy or very irritable, or if breathing becomes difficult [2]. q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough with a hoarse voice and noisy breathing is croup — an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe, usually caused by a virus, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Keep your son calm and comfortable, since the cough and the noise can get worse when a child is upset or crying [3]. Offer fluids if he has a fever, and you can give the usual fever medicine [4]. Water can help ease a cough, whether he drinks it or you add moisture to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [6]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four [6].

Get help if you are worried about his breathing — croup can rarely become serious and interfere with breathing [1]. Also watch his breathing, his colour and how he seems in himself, as these can show he is getting worse [4].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, and they usually start within 10–15 days of being bitten by an infected mosquito, according to the WHO [4]. Because these symptoms are not specific, getting tested early is important [4]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [4].

Severe symptoms include extreme tiredness and fatigue, impaired consciousness, multiple convulsions, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, jaundice (yellowing of the eyes and skin), and abnormal bleeding [4]. People with severe symptoms should get emergency care right away [4]. Getting treatment early for mild malaria can stop the infection from becoming severe [4].

If you travelled to an area where malaria is common, you may need to take medicines to prevent the disease, taken before you leave, during travel, and for a short period after you return, according to MedlinePlus [3].

Fainting during exercise needs to be checked, and the SEUP says a faint that happens during physical exercise is a reason to go to the emergency department [5]. While you get help, lay your teenager down with their legs raised and their head turned to the side so they breathe more easily, according to the SEUP [6]. If they are still unconscious, the SEUP advises placing them in the recovery position on their side and calling the emergency services [5].

The SEUP also lists these as reasons to be seen in the emergency department: if it takes more than 3 to 5 minutes to come round, if the faint happened during exercise or effort or while sitting, or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the arms and legs, or passing urine without control at the end [5]. The NHS says to get immediate help if someone cannot be woken within 1 minute, is not breathing, has not fully recovered or has trouble with speech or movement, has chest pain or a pounding, fluttering or irregular heartbeat, has seriously hurt themselves, or is shaking or jerking [3].

After a period of rest, children usually recover quickly, within a couple of minutes [6]. The SEUP says faints generally do not come from serious medical problems and need no special tests, and that children who tend to faint should drink more fluids, especially when they exercise [4].

q: my child says everything looks blurry after getting hit in the face with a ball

text:
Blurry vision after a hit to the face can be a sign of concussion, a temporary brain injury that happens when a hit to the head or body makes the brain move inside the skull [5]. A concussion can happen even without passing out, and symptoms can take hours or days to appear [5].

While you get your child seen, keep them resting and avoid activities that need a lot of concentration, such as screens or studying, since these can bring symptoms back or make them worse [4]. Do not let them rub the eye or try to remove anything from it [1].

Get help right away if there is neck pain, double vision, loss of consciousness, seizure, repeated vomiting, a headache that is severe or getting worse, or weakness, tingling or burning in the arms or legs [3]. Also get medical help for decreased vision, a lot of eye pain or sensitivity to light, or any changes to sight after an eye injury [1][6].

q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature get better within 1 to 4 days [5]. The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the number down by itself [3].

Keep offering plenty of liquids in small amounts often, and don't force food if they refuse it [3]. Dress them lightly and keep the room comfortably cool — don't bundle them up [3]. For the fever, you can give acetaminophen (Tylenol) every 4 to 6 hours, or ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours; know your child's weight before giving either [4]. If they won't take the Tylenol, you can try ibuprofen instead [4]. Don't give aspirin to a child [4]. Don't bathe them in cold water or use wet cloths — it's unpleasant and doesn't help [3].

Get help if your child has a seizure or fit, or seems very unwell [5].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105°C is not possible — a thermometer reading that high means the thermometer is faulty or was misread, because a high temperature in children is 38C (100.4 °F) or more [1]. A fever is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, and many things can cause it, from common childhood illnesses like chickenpox and tonsillitis to vaccinations [3]. It usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1].

You can usually look after them at home [4]. Do give them plenty of fluids, give them food if they want it, check on them regularly including during the night, and keep them at home [4]. Give them either paracetamol or ibuprofen if they're distressed or uncomfortable — check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable for your child, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you're not sure [4]. Get medical advice if you're worried about your child, or if the paracetamol or ibuprofen is not helping [4].

Get help if your child has other signs of illness such as a rash along with the high temperature, has a high temperature that's lasted 5 days or more, does not want to eat or is not their usual self and you're worried, or is dehydrated — such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when they're crying [3].

text:
Itchy skin at night has several possible causes, and scabies is one of them: the itch of scabies is often worse at night, with itchy lines and bumps on the fingers, wrists, arms and legs, according to the WHO [2]. If it is scabies, it should be treated quickly to stop it spreading, and it is spread through close skin contact [5]. If you are not sure what is causing it, have your child seen by your doctor so the right treatment can be started.

Bathe in cool water and pat the skin dry without rubbing, and dress in loose clothes [3].

q: how long does flu last in toddlers
text:
Most toddlers recover from flu within about a week, according to the WHO [5]. The fever and other symptoms usually settle in that time without needing medical care, though the cough can be severe and last two weeks or more [5].

While your child is ill: keep them home so they don't pass it on, let them rest, and give plenty of fluids [4]. You can use over-the-counter medicine to bring down fever or aches, but cough and flu medicine should not be given to children under 6 unless a health care provider advises it [6].

Get medical care if symptoms get worse, or if your child has severe symptoms [4]. The WHO lists children under 5 as being at higher risk, so seek care if you are worried [4].

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is very common and usually nothing to worry about; it normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [5]. It is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu [4].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, rest, and avoid smoking or smoky places [5]. She can also gargle with warm, salty water — half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out [5].

You do not normally need antibiotics, because they will not usually relieve the symptoms or speed up recovery [7]. A pharmacist can give advice, and can supply antibiotics if it could be a bacterial infection [7].

See a pharmacist if she needs help for the sore throat [7]. See a doctor if it does not improve after a week, if she often gets sore throats, or if she has a lump in her mouth or neck or a mouth ulcer lasting more than 3 weeks [7]. Ask for an urgent appointment now if you are worried, if she has a very high temperature or feels hot, cold or shivery, if she has signs of dehydration such as peeing less than usual or dark, strong-smelling pee, or if she has a weakened immune system [7]. Get emergency help now if she has difficulty breathing or cannot swallow, is drooling, is making a high-pitched sound as she breathes, or has severe symptoms getting worse quickly [7].

q: he has an inhaler but I dont know when to use it
text:
The main treatment for asthma is medicine breathed in with an inhaler, and a doctor, nurse or pharmacist will show you how to use yours [3]. If your child is having an asthma attack, sit them up straight to help their breathing and try to stay calm [2]. Use the reliever inhaler if you have one: with a blue reliever inhaler, take 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds until they feel better, up to a maximum of 10 puffs, shaking the inhaler between each puff and using a spacer if you have one [2]. If it is an AIR or MART inhaler, take 1 puff every 1 to 3 minutes until they feel better, up to a maximum of 6 puffs [2]. If their own asthma action plan gives a different maximum, follow that plan [2].

Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the child turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [1]. Call your local emergency number if they start to feel worse at any time, do not feel better after the maximum dose of the reliever inhaler, or do not have an inhaler [2]. If symptoms are no better after 10 minutes and help has not arrived, use the inhaler again, up to the same maximum dose [2]. Even after recovering from an attack, see your doctor within 2 days to discuss treatment and prevent another attack [2]. See your doctor if treatments are not helping, the inhaler is needed more often, or you need advice about using it [4].

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text:
It is usually normal for a 9-month-old not to have teeth yet: first teeth usually show between 4 and 8 months of age, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Some babies are simply later than that.

Until the first tooth appears, wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal, and do not put them to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. As soon as the first tooth shows, switch to a soft toothbrush [4]. Once there are teeth, brush them at least twice a day, especially before bed, and take your child to a dentist every 6 months [1].

Ask your child's health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4].

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Chickenpox is very contagious, and a child is contagious from 1 to 2 days before the rash starts until all the spots have crusted over, according to the CDC [3]. Children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of chickenpox [1].

Keep him home while he is still contagious — that means until every lesion has scabbed over [3]. If he was vaccinated and gets chickenpox, he may have spots that do not crust; in that case he is contagious until no new spots have appeared for 24 hours [3].

For the itching, calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help, and acetaminophen can treat the fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Do not give aspirin for chickenpox, because that combination can cause Reye syndrome [6].

text:
Yes, she should be watched — a bump to the head can cause a concussion, and symptoms may not show up right away, according to the CDC [3]. Keep an eye on how she acts and feels over the next hours and days, and if her symptoms get worse, tell her healthcare provider [3].

Get help immediately if she has any of these: a headache that gets worse or does not go away, repeated vomiting or nausea, convulsions or seizures, trouble waking up, one pupil larger than the other, slurred speech, weakness or numbness in the arms or legs, loss of coordination, or increased confusion, restlessness, or agitation [2]. In an infant or toddler, also get help if she will not stop crying and cannot be consoled, or will not nurse or eat [4].

q: my baby is 7 months and has been warm since last night, 101.8 F
text:
A temperature of 101.8 F (38.8 C (101.8 °F)) is a fever, and in a 7-month-old this is usually caused by a common infection the body is fighting, according to the NHS [3]. It usually settles within 1 to 4 days [3].

You can usually care for your baby at home. Offer plenty of fluids — if you are breastfeeding, keep feeding as normal — and watch for signs of dehydration such as fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, or no tears when crying [2][5]. Give food if they want it, check on them regularly including through the night, and keep them at home [2]. If they are distressed or uncomfortable, you can give either paracetamol or ibuprofen — check the packaging or leaflet to be sure the medicine suits your child, or ask a pharmacist or doctor if unsure [2]. Do not undress or sponge them to cool them, and do not bundle them in too many clothes or blankets [1].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if paracetamol or ibuprofen is not helping [2]. Also seek help if your baby has a rash along with the fever, is not eating or is not their usual self, or is dehydrated [1][5].

q: my daughter has diarrhea since yesterday and doesnt want much food
text:
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the stomach and intestines, and diarrhea is one of its main symptoms; it is usually not serious in healthy people, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most people get better on their own with rest and plenty of fluids and electrolytes [2]. Offer fluids often in small amounts, and keep offering food — a child who does not want much food can still drink.

Contact a provider right away if your daughter has any of these: a change in her mental state, such as irritability or lack of energy; diarrhea lasting more than a day; frequent loose stools; vomiting often; severe pain in her belly or rectum; signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying; or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus [3].

q: is the MMR vaccine safe for my baby I read online it causes autism
text: No, the MMR vaccine does not cause autism. Many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [5]. The American Academy of Pediatrics, the National Academy of Medicine, and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have all concluded that the benefits of vaccines outweigh their risks [3]. The MMR is a live but weakened virus vaccine; unless a child's immune system is weakened, it is unlikely to cause the illness it protects against [3]. Research over many years has also shown no link between thimerosal, a preservative once used in vaccines, and autism [3]. If you are worried about your child having a vaccine, or are not sure whether they can have it, speak to your doctor [7].

q: my baby has yellow skin, is that normal at 3 days old
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Baby with yellow skin or eyes: urgent appointment today. If under 24 hours old, very sleepy, not feeding, feverish or no wet nappies, go to emergency now
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

It is common for a baby's yellow skin to be most noticeable around 3 days old, and jaundice in babies is usually harmless and gets better without treatment [1]. It usually takes around 2 weeks to go [1].

Encouraging your baby to feed regularly, around 8 to 12 times a day, can help them get better more quickly; if they're sleepy, try waking them for feeds [6]. Ask your doctor or midwife for advice if you're finding it difficult to feed your baby, or you're not sure they are feeding enough [6].

Because your baby is under 3 months old, they need to be assessed by a doctor the same day. While you arrange that, keep feeding them regularly and watch for these signs, which mean getting help straight away: being sleepier than normal or difficult to wake, not feeding, being floppy or stiff, or having jerking or twitching movements, a high temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or more or a low temperature of 36C (96.8 °F) or less, feeling hot or cold to the touch or shivering, no wet nappies, or difficulty breathing [1]. Also get help if their pee is dark yellow or brown or their poo is a pale creamy colour [1].

q: she has a fever and cold hands and feet, is that normal
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Cold hands and feet in a child with fever: it may be poor circulation, get it checked
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day [1].

For an older child, a high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1]. Unusually cold hands and feet are listed as a sign needing immediate action [1].

While you get help: do not undress your child or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [1]. Do not give aspirin to children under 16 [1]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [1]. Do not give paracetamol under 2 months, or ibuprofen under 3 months, under 5kg, with chickenpox, dehydration, or asthma unless a doctor recommends it [1]. The dose depends on age and weight.

Get help today if there is also a rash, a fever lasting 5 days or more, they are not eating or not themselves, or signs of dehydration such as nappies not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [1].

q: my baby fell off the bed and bumped his head (age: 8 months) (weight: 18 lbs)
text:
18 lb = 8.2 kg.

A bump on the head from a fall is a head injury, and most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous, according to the SEUP [3]. Your baby may have a headache, nausea, vomiting or be sleepy [1].

What to do now: keep an eye on him for the first 24 hours after the knock to spot any serious symptoms [3]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is advisable to wake him every 4 hours [6]. He does not need any special food — carry on with his usual feeding according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the doses your doctor indicates [6]. Rest physically and mentally for 24 to 48 hours, depending on how hard the knock was, with no physical activity or screens, then return to normal activities gradually [4].

Get help at the emergency department if he has any of these: a severe, worsening headache that does not improve with the usual medicine; repeated vomiting; confusion or disorientation, or in a very small child, being irritable or hard to wake; changes in usual behaviour, difficulty speaking or walking; blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]. Also go if his behaviour or mood worries you, or if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

q: my daughter has hives after eating eggs but no trouble breathing
text:
Hives are raised, itchy red patches that move around — they fade in one spot as they appear in another. In childhood, most hives are caused by an infection, and an allergic cause is less common, according to the SEUP [1].

Hives can come with swelling of the hands, feet, elbows or face, and only rarely with trouble breathing or swallowing [1]. Since your daughter is breathing normally, the SEUP's advice for hives is to see your doctor, who can look at the cause and decide on treatment [1].

Go to the emergency department if she develops difficulty breathing or swallowing, or swelling of the face, lips or tongue [1].

q: she feels hot but the thermometer says 98.6
text:
A temperature of 98.6 °F is normal, not a fever — a fever is a body temperature higher than normal, and normal is usually around 98.6 °F (37 °C (98.6 °F)) [6]. A high temperature is usually considered to be 38 °C (100.4 °F) or above [4].

If she feels hot to touch but the thermometer reads normal, the reading may be off. If she has just had a bath, been wrapped in a blanket, been very active, been cuddling a hot water bottle, or is wearing a lot of clothes, let her cool down for a few minutes — but do not let her get cold or shivery — then take her temperature again [2]. Use a digital thermometer in the armpit, held in place as long as the manufacturer's instructions say [1][3].

A fever itself is not a disease; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an illness or infection [6]. If she does have a fever, it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1]. Make sure she drinks enough liquids to prevent dehydration [6].

banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Swallowed an object or something is stuck in the throat (batteries, magnets, a fish bone)
text:
A swallowed magnet needs medical assessment, and more than one magnet is the case that matters most: swallowing several magnetic pieces can cause twisted bowel [5]. If you can see a solid object in the mouth and can reach it, take it out — never blindly, as that could make things worse — and do not try to make them vomit or give water, milk, oil or food [2].

Keep them away from any remaining magnets and try to work out how many were swallowed [2]. A single magnet usually causes no problem, but several can [5].

Go now if there is strong, continuous belly pain that keeps getting worse, repeated vomiting, or vomit that is green, brown or bloody, or black tarry or bloody stools [3][4]. Also go if the belly is tense, hard or swollen [3].

They can include swelling or pain where the injection was given, a high temperature, and a rash — either at the injection site or more widespread, usually appearing within 1 month of vaccination [3]. q: my baby has a cough and sounds very congested when sleeping
text:
A cough and a blocked, congested nose are common in babies, and the NHS says growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how a baby sleeps [6].

Keep the nose clear and keep feeding as usual. If you're breastfeeding, your baby may doze off for short periods during a feed — carry on feeding until they've finished or are fully asleep [2]. For sleep, the safest place is a separate cot or Moses basket free from toys, blankets and pillows [4]. If you share a bed, make sure they sleep on a firm, flat mattress on their back, keep pillows, sheets and blankets away from them, and don't swaddle them — baby sleeping bags are safer [1].

Get urgent help if you're worried about your baby or think they might be ill [7]. Call your local emergency number if your baby stops breathing, will not wake up, is struggling for breath, is stiff, shaking or jerking, turns pale, blue or grey, or is limp, floppy or not responding as usual [7].

text:
Ear infections are very common in children and often get better on their own within 3 days, according to the NHS [3]. Tugging or pulling at the ear, crying more than usual and being irritable are signs to look for when a child is too young to say their ear hurts [1][4].

For the pain, the SEUP says to give ibuprofen or paracetamol regularly every 6-8 hours for the first 1-2 days, before the pain builds up [6]. Do not put anything in the ear to ease the pain, and keep the ear dry, especially if it has been discharging [6]. If he is a baby, frequent nasal washes with saline help [6]. If an antibiotic has been prescribed, follow the dose, interval and duration exactly [6].

See your doctor: the SEUP advises this for babies with ear infection, and the NHS says to get help if your child has a high temperature or does not feel well enough for normal activities [3][6].

q: my 3 year old keeps vomiting every time he drinks water
text:
A child who vomits every time he drinks is at risk of losing fluids, so the aim is to get liquid in slowly rather than in one go. If he is having trouble keeping liquids down, try small sips of water or sucking on ice chips, according to MedlinePlus [1].

Keep offering small amounts more often than usual, and give regular small sips of rehydration solution to replace lost fluids — your pharmacist can recommend one [3]. Carry on with his usual diet, and do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [3].

Get help if he vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even when he takes nothing; if the vomit is green, contains blood or looks like coffee grounds; if he is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or passes little urine; or if he has severe tummy pain or a headache [2].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation, and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3]. The main sign is stool that is harder and less frequent than usual, sometimes with tummy pain, bloating, or a feeling of not having finished [2]. Pain when passing, and a little blood on the stool, can come from a small anal tear [2][4].

What helps: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass [1]. Add more fiber — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables — and don't replace fruit with juice, since juice has little fiber [1]. Keep a regular routine and don't let him hold it in when he needs to go [1]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without asking your pediatrician [1].

See your pediatrician if the constipation comes with bad tummy pain, if he is very down and complaining a lot, if there is blood in the stool, or if he vomits many times and can't keep down solids or liquids [1].

q: my baby has been vomiting for six hours but still wants to breastfeed
text:
A baby who is vomiting but still wants to breastfeed can keep breastfeeding — the SEUP says to keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if the baby asks for it [2]. Offer smaller amounts more often to lower the risk of vomiting, and don't force food [2][3]. Avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices; sports drinks are not suitable for a child with diarrhoea [2]. The vomiting usually settles on its own in less than a week [3].

Get help if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds; vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without taking anything; the vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like brown coffee grounds; is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine; or has severe tummy pain or a headache [4].

A fever in a baby this young is a temperature of 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher, according to the NHS [3]. A normal temperature varies a little from child to child, and a high temperature is 38 °C (100.4 °F) or more [3].

q: my son passed out after standing in the sun for a long time

text:
First, do what the warning above says.

Heat exhaustion can happen after being out in the heat too long, and it needs to be cooled down and given fluids [7]. Move your son to a cool place, remove unnecessary clothing, and give him plenty of water to drink — an isotonic sports drink or oral rehydration powder mixed with water also helps replace salt lost through sweating [4]. Cool his skin by spraying or sponging him with cool water and fanning him; cold packs wrapped in a cloth under the armpits or on the neck work too [4]. Stay with him until he is better — he should start to cool down and feel better within 30 minutes [4]. While you wait for help, wrap him in a cool, wet sheet, or fan him or sponge him down with cold water [5]. If he loses consciousness, put him in the recovery position and check his breathing and pulse [5].

q: my 6 year old has a cough that is worse at night
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the pattern of the cough helps tell them apart. With croup, a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing usually come on after a few days of cold-like symptoms and are often worse at night [3]. Asthma causes a persistent cough, especially at night, sometimes with wheezing or chest tightness [1]. Whooping cough starts like a cold, then brings coughing bouts that are worse at night and may end in a "whoop" or vomiting [4].

If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your health care provider right away [6]. Ask for an urgent appointment if you think your child may have croup, or if they are getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [3]. Get medical help right away for severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [5].

text:
A knock on the head is a common injury in children, and the skull is hard and protects the brain, according to MedlinePlus [4]. After a head injury, the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1].

Keep your child resting, both physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was; during this time no sport and no screens, and return to normal activities gradually [5]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen for headache — the dose depends on your child's weight [5].

Go to the emergency department if your child has any of the symptoms above, or a behaviour or mood that worries you, or is under three months old, or fell from more than one metre [3]. q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are often eczema, a common skin condition in young children that causes dry, itchy skin [1]. Scratching can make the skin red, swollen and itch even more [2].

To help: apply moisturising treatments (emollients) at least twice a day, and keep moisturising even when the skin improves [5]. Wash with an emollient instead of soap, avoid things that make it worse such as soap, washing detergent, some fabrics or pets, and keep your child cool, since being hot makes eczema more itchy [5]. Keep nails short, and put anti-scratch mittens on babies to prevent damage from scratching [5].

See your doctor if your child has symptoms of atopic eczema, or if treatments are not helping [4]. Get help urgently if the skin is blistered, crusty, leaking fluid or has spots filled with pus; if it is painful, swollen or feels warm; if it suddenly gets worse or gets bigger; or if your child has a high temperature or feels generally unwell — these can be signs of infection or a more serious condition called eczema herpeticum [4].

text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: symptoms often start after physical effort, and in preschool children the main cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections, according to the SEUP [2][7]. Get help if your child has severe trouble breathing, intense coughing, or pale or bluish colour in the face, lips or nails — seek medical help immediately [4]. A bluish colour around the lips means the oxygen in the blood is low [7].

q: my 4 year old has earache after a cold
text:
Earache after a cold is often caused by an infection of the middle ear, behind the eardrum. It usually happens as a complication of an upper respiratory cold with a lot of nasal mucus, according to the SEUP [5].

Keep the nose clear and give plenty to drink. If your child has a fever, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen; the dose depends on their weight, and PediBot's dose calculator can work it out for you.

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
text:
A blocked nose and trouble feeding in a baby is often a cold: sneezing, a stuffy nose, runny mucus, sore throat and cough are the usual symptoms, and they can last 10 to 14 days [2].

To help at home, keep the nose clear with nasal washes, and feed in small, frequent amounts to keep feeding and hydration good [1]. Hold your baby in a semi-upright position to make breathing easier, and give fever medicine if there is fever [1]. Keep your baby away from tobacco smoke, and wash your hands often to avoid passing the virus on [1].

Go to the emergency department if your baby breathes worse or faster, stops breathing for a few seconds or the lips turn blue-purple, has trouble feeding, refuses feeds or vomits, has a dry mouth and tongue or fewer wet nappies, is very floppy or whiny, or has a very high fever [7].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
A stomach ache with no appetite is common in children, and the NHS lists tummy pain among the symptoms of norovirus, a stomach bug that usually gets better in about 2 days [4]. Norovirus symptoms usually start suddenly and may include feeling sick, being sick, and diarrhoea, sometimes with a high temperature, headache or body aches [4].

Offer small sips of fluid often so they stay hydrated, and let them eat little and often if they want to — do not force food [2]. If they are active, gaining weight and seem well, they are getting enough to eat, and it helps to look at what they eat over a week rather than in a day [3].

See a doctor if the stomach ache is severe or keeps getting worse, if they cannot keep fluids down, if they are drowsy or unusually unwell, or if they have blood in their poo or vomit.

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most insect bites are harmless, though they can be uncomfortable, and mosquito bites usually itch [5]. The bite should get better in a few days [1].

To ease the itching and swelling, put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, and keep the area raised if it's swollen [1]. Do not let her scratch the bites, as they could get infected, and do not use home remedies such as bicarbonate of soda [7].

See a pharmacist if the skin around a bite feels hot or looks red, if it's painful, if the area looks swollen, or if there's pus or fluid coming out of it [7]. text:
दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण होता है, और इसे ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) से ठीक किया जाना चाहिए — यह साफ पानी, चीनी और नमक का घोल है [3]। विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार, इसके साथ ज़िंक की घुलनशील गोलियाँ भी दी जाती हैं, जो दस्त की अवधि कम करती हैं और नतीजे बेहतर बनाती हैं [3]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को ORS घोल पिलाएँ [1]। ज़िंक सप्लीमेंट दस्त के दौरान देने से एपिसोड की अवधि लगभग 25% कम होती है और मल की मात्रा में लगभग 30% कमी आती है [1]। खाना खाने से रोकें नहीं — पोषक तत्वों से भरपूर खाना, जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है, दस्त के दौरान भी जारी रखें, क्योंकि इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें, खासकर अगर दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहें, मल में खून आए, या निर्जलीकरण के संकेत दिखें [1]।
sources: [1] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Prevention and treatment", p. 1 — https://www.who
[3] WHO — "Diarrhoeal disease", section "Overview", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/news-room/f

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह में छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे हुए दाने निकल आते हैं; ये अक्सर हल्के होते हैं और 7 से 10 दिन में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं, बताता है NHS [3][1]। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं [1]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने और बुखार हो सकते हैं [5]।

अभी के लिए: ठंडे तरल पदार्थ दें ताकि मुँह को आराम मिले और पानी की कमी न हो — खट्टे पेय जैसे फलों का रस न दें; दही जैसा मुलायम खाना दें और गरम, नमकीन व मसालेदार खाना न दें [1]। मुँह या गले में दर्द के लिए पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार दें।

अगर मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या बच्चा साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ करे, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [1] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "How to treat hand, foot and mou
[3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout
[5] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of chickenpox", p. 1 —
[6] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Raised, itchy spots or patches"

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
मेडलाइनप्लस के अनुसार, शिशुओं में पेशाब कम आना और मुँह सूखना निर्जलीकरण के संकेत हैं [5]। ऐसे में तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [5]।

अभी ओआरएस (मौखिक पुनर्जलीकरण घोल) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार देना सबसे ज़रूरी है, क्योंकि निर्जलीकरण रोकना ही मुख्य इलाज है [1]। घोल पैकेट पर लिखे निर्देशों के अनुसार साफ़ पानी में मिलाएँ — आधा लीटर या एक लीटर, पैकेट के हिसाब से — और अच्छी तरह हिलाएँ [7]। स्वाद आँसू जैसा होना चाहिए, न ज़्यादा मीठा न ज़्यादा नमकीन; 24 घंटे बाद बचा घोल फेंक दें [7]। घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक्स न दें [1]। स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और माँगने पर उससे भी ज़्यादा बार जारी रखें [8]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत सुस्त हो, बेचैन या चिड़चिड़ा हो, आँखें धँसी लगें, या पानी पीने से इनकार करे, तो तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लें [1][3]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर ध्यान देना ज़रूरी है, और SEUP के मुताबिक चोट के बाद 24 से 48 घंटे तक शारीरिक और मानसिक आराम ज़रूरी है — इस दौरान खेल-कूद और मोबाइल, टैबलेट या वीडियो गेम जैसी चीज़ें नहीं [1]।

घर पर इन लक्षणों पर नज़र रखें, जो हालत बिगड़ने का संकेत हो सकते हैं: तेज़ या लगातार बढ़ता सिरदर्द, या ऐसा सिरदर्द जो आम दर्द की दवा (पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन) से ठीक न हो; बार-बार उल्टी; बेचैनी, भ्रम या ध्यान न लगना; बहुत छोटे बच्चों में चिड़चिड़ापन या नींद से जगाना मुश्किल होना; रोज़ के व्यवहार में बदलाव, बोलने या चलने में दिक्कत; और नाक या कान से खून या साफ़ तरल निकलना [1]।

दवा की खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है — पैकेट पर लिखी बात देखें या अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें [5]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO PUEDE V

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
बच्चे का कब्ज़ में पॉटी करते समय रोना आम बात है — कब्ज़ उन कारणों में से एक है जिनसे बच्चा रो सकता है [2]।

कब्ज़ में पॉटी करते समय दर्द हो सकता है, इसलिए बच्चा रोता है। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे शांत या ध्यान भटका कर चुप नहीं करा पा रहे हैं, या उसका रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]।

अगर बच्चा रोते समय पीला पड़ जाए, पसीना आए, सुस्त लगे या दूध/खाना लेना बंद कर दे, या बुखार हो, उल्टी हो या पॉटी में खून आए, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।
sources: [2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना बुखार के बढ़ने का संकेत है — SEUP के अनुसार, जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और खासकर हाथों-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा रंग (कटिस मार्मोराटा) दिखना सामान्य है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है, तब बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]।

बुखार खुद कोई बीमारी नहीं है — यह शरीर के संक्रमण से लड़ने का संकेत है, और ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसका कारण साधारण, विशेषकर वायरल, संक्रमण होता है [1][4]। बुखार में बच्चे को बेचैनी, कम भूख, थकान या सिरदर्द हो सकता है [2]। बुखार के दौरान बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल पदार्थ पिलाते रहें ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। अगर बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो, तो स्वास्थ्यकर्मी पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी बिना पर्चे की दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है — PediBot का डोज़ कैलकुलेटर सिर्फ़ पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन के लिए है।
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[4] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ ES LA FIEBRE?", p. 1 —

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना गंभीरता के संकेतों में गिना जाता है — ऐसे लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। साथ ही बच्चे को खाने-पीने में रुचि न होना, स्तनपान न करना, साँस लेते समय पसलियों का अंदर खिंचना, सीने से कराहने या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आना, और त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक भी गंभीरता के लक्षण हैं [2]।

जब तक मदद पहुँचे, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसकी साँस और जागने की हालत पर नज़र रखें। बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]। बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना अकेले भी इस बात का संकेत हो सकता है कि वह पर्याप्त तरल नहीं पी रहा — एनएचएस के अनुसार पेशाब का गाढ़ा रंग या कम मात्रा तब हो सकती है जब पर्याप्त पानी न पिया गया हो [3]।

अब जो करें: बच्चे को बार-बार थोड़ा-थोड़ा तरल दें, खासकर पानी, ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न रहे [4]। अगर दस्त या उल्टी भी हो रही है, तो घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक न दें — तैयार ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन दें, और दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना डॉक्टर से पूछे न दें [1]।

डॉक्टर से कब मिलें: अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, पेशाब कम करे या आँखें धँसी दिखें; बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो, सुस्त हो या जवाब देने में कमी हो; खाना-पीना मना करे; पेट में लगातार या तेज़ दर्द हो या मल में बहुत खून आए — तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाएँ [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "Ofrecer en pe
[3] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "Urinary tract infections (UTI
[4] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "How to prevent urinary tract

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें या स्पंज न करें [2]। बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें, और पैरासिटामोल व आइबुप्रोफेन बारी-बारी से न दें जब तक डॉक्टर या नर्स न कहें [2]। 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल न दें, और 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या निर्जलीकरण वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है — वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार दें।

रास्ते में: बच्चे को करवट पर लिटाएँ और मुँह में कुछ न डालें [1]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Paracetamol bukhar aur takleef mein madad karta hai, aur ise har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai — din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi, AEPap ke mutabiq [3]. Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ke liye sahi matra bacche ke vazan par nirbhar karti hai, umar par nahi [3].

PediBot ka dose calculator sirf paracetamol aur ibuprofen ke liye hai, isliye aap wahan apne bacche ka vazan daal kar sahi matra nikaal sakte hain [3]. Ibuprofen bhi ek vikalp hai, har 6 se 8 ghante mein, lekin agar lagatar ulti ho rahi ho to ise na dein [3]. Pehle paracetamol se shuru karna behtar mana jata hai [3].

Dhyan rahe: do alag antitérmicos ko baari-baari na dein; sirf tab badlein jab 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar tez ho aur takleef kam na ho [3]. Aspirin ya sharab se badan ponchhna istemal na karein [5].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi aksar asthma ka ek lakshan ho sakta hai — MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. Bronquiolitis mein bhi raat ki khansi ho sakti hai, aur zyada tar mamle halke hote hain jo ghar par sambhal sakte hain [5].

Ghar par: kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer rakhein, naak ki saline boondein ya spray dein, aur bachche ko khoob taral (paani, doodh) pilayein [6]. SEUP ke mutabik khansi ke syrup, mucolytic, corticoide, antibiotic ya respiratory physiotherapy bronquiolitis mein faydemand nahi hain [2]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein [6].

Doctor se turant milein agar: saans lene mein sakht takleef ya tez saans, seene ka dhadakna/andar dhansna, hothon ke aas-paas neela rang, khansi lagatar aur bolne mein dikkat [3]; ya doodh peene mein dikkat, rang badalna, bukhar [5].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Mere bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli — in lakshanon ke saath, yeh heat rash (prickly heat) jaisa lag sakta hai: chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling, aur halki sujan [6]. Yeh aam taur par harmless hota hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Ab kya karein: sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina na aaye aur rash na bade [6]. Dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahayein [6]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez — geela kapda ya ice pack (towel mein lipta hua) — 20 minute tak lagayein, aur rash ko kuraidne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Doctor se kab milein: agar aap sure nahi hain ki yeh heat rash hai, to doosre rashes ko dekhein [6]. Agar bachche ke munh ke aas-paas sujan ho ya saans lene mein dikkat ho, to turant emergency help lein [5].

Is dauran khel-kood aur electronic devices (tablet, video games, smartphone) se door rakhein [1]. Uske baad hi dhire-dhire normal kaam par wapas laayein [1].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kuch bachche kabz ki wajah se rote hain — yeh NHS kehta hai ki constipation un karanon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bachcha ro sakta hai [3]. Kabz ke saath potty karte waqt rehna mushkil ho sakta hai, isliye pehle yeh dekhein ki kabz theek ho.

Agar bachcha 3 ghante se zyada, hafte mein 3 din, kam se kam 1 hafta se rota hai aur warna sehatmand hai, to yeh colic ho sakta hai [3]. Colic aksar dopahar aur shaam ko zyada hota hai, aur aam taur par 3 se 4 mahine ki umar tak theek ho jata hai [3]. Colic mein bachcha apni mutthi band karta hai, chehra laal karta hai, ghutne pet ki taraf uthata hai ya kamar modta hai, pet gudgudata hai ya gas zyada hoti hai [3].

Agar samajh na aaye ki kya galat hai, to apne doctor se baat karein [3]. Turant madad lein agar bachcha: mirgi ka daura (seizure) aaye; hont, zubaan ya skin neeli, grey, pale ya dhabbedar ho; behosh, dheela ya aam se zyada na jaag raha ho; saans lene mein dikkat ho (ghurghur ya pasliyan andar khinchti dikhein), saans phool rahi ho ya bahut tez ho; bahut zyada ulti (projectile) ho; temperature bahut zyada ya bahut kam ho; aisa daane ho jo dabane par gayab na ho; ya pichhle 8 ghante mein peshab na kiya ho [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai

text:
Mere bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai — SEUP ke mutabik ye ek aisi nishani hai jiske liye turant emergency department jaana chahiye [1]. Ghabraayein nahi, bas jaldi madad lein.

Jab tak madad pahunchti hai, bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, kapde dheele karein, aur unke saans lene par nazar rakhein [1]. Kuch bhi muh mein na daalein [1].

SEUP ke mutabik saans lene ki dikkat ki gambhir nishaniyan yeh hain: pasliyan saaf dikhna, bahut tez saans lena, saans mein rukawat aana, ya bachcha sust aur neend mein rehna [1]. Skin, hoth ya jeebh ka neela ya grey hona bhi ek gambhir nishani hai [1].

NHS ke mutabik agar bachcha theek se doodh ya khana nahi le raha, ya bahut thak gaya hai, to bhi turant madad lein [5].

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
Mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai — tez saans lena (rapid breathing) kai cheezon ka lakshan ho sakta hai, jaise bronchiolitis, RSV ya pneumonia [3][4][6].

Abhi kya karein: bachche ko aaram dein aur paani/feed chalu rakhein. Agar wo doodh peeta hai to thoda-thoda, baar-baar dein — kam mat karein [3][4]. Saans lene mein madad ke liye unhe seedha aur aaram se rakhein.

Dhyan dein: agar saans lene mein rukawat ho, seene ki pasliyan andar khinch rahi hon, naak ke aas-paas se awaaz aaye, ya bachcha bahut thak gaya ho, sust ho, ya doodh peena kam kar de — to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [3][6]. Agar hoth, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho jaye, saans lene mein ruk-ruk ke pause aaye, ya bachcha bilkul sust ho kar na jaage — to turant emergency help lein [3].

Bachche ki saans ki takleef ke liye koi ghar ka ilaaj nahi hai; doctor hi sahi jaanch kar sakta hai [6].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that's worse at night is common with whooping cough: after about a week, children get coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. The cough may last for several weeks or months [3].

Keep the room and bedding from making your child too hot, and ask a pharmacist about cough medicine — but some cough medicines should not be given to children under 12 years old [1].

Get urgent help if the cough is very bad or quickly gets worse, your child feels very unwell, has chest pain, has swollen and painful glands in the side of the neck, finds it hard to breathe, or is coughing up blood [1]. Also get medical care right away if your child has a pause in breathing or starts to turn blue [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash of red pimples all over the body in a small child can have several causes, and the NHS says scabies in infants and small children may cause a more widespread rash, including the palms, soles, ankles and sometimes the scalp [4]. The NHS also says that spots appearing on a baby's upper body, scalp, cheeks, forehead and chin up to 6 weeks after birth could be baby acne, which does not need treatment and usually gets better after a few weeks or months [3].

If the rash is itchy, scabies typically causes severe itch, and a doctor can recognise it by its typical features [4].

Get help urgently if your child's lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly become swollen, if they are breathing very fast or struggling to breathe, if their throat feels tight or they are struggling to swallow, if their skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale, if they suddenly become very confused, drowsy or dizzy, if they faint and cannot be woken, or if they become limp, floppy or not responding like they normally do — these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction and may need immediate treatment in hospital [7].

q: should I give polio drops if my baby already had injection
text:
The polio vaccine is given as part of the routine schedule, and what your baby needs next depends on which vaccines they have already had and when they were born [2]. The six-in-one vaccine, which protects against polio, is offered at eight, twelve and sixteen weeks old [2].

If your child missed a vaccination, contact your GP to catch up, and they will advise what vaccination your child should get and when [1][3]. It is important that vaccines are given on time for the best protection [3].

Before vaccination, tell the doctor or nurse if your baby has a very high temperature, vomiting or diarrhoea on the day of the appointment, has had convulsions or fits, had a bad reaction to a previous immunisation, is allergic to anything, has a bleeding disorder, has had or is having treatment for cancer, has an illness that affects the immune system such as leukaemia, HIV or AIDS, takes medicine that affects the immune system, or has any other serious illness [5].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, and it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week than in a single day, according to the NHS [6]. Keep offering a variety of foods and go back to foods they refused before — children's tastes change, and it may take many attempts before they accept something [6]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and don't force or leave meals until they're too hungry or tired [3]. Two healthy snacks a day between meals is plenty, and don't use food as a reward [3].

If your child is active and gaining weight, and they seem well, then they're getting enough to eat [6]. As long as they eat some food from the 4 main food groups, you do not need to worry [6].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A congested chest with a whistling sound when breathing is called wheezing, and in a 6-month-old it often comes with a cold-like illness such as bronchiolitis or RSV, according to the NHS [2][4]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in about 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding your baby as normally as you can, in smaller amounts more often if they are finding it hard to feed, and keep them upright and calm while you travel to be seen [2][4]. If they are feeding much less than normal or have had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, that also needs urgent attention [2][4].

Get help right away if your child is having difficulty breathing — grunting noises, their tummy sucking under their ribs, or breathing quickly — if there are pauses when they breathe, if their skin, tongue or lips are blue or grey, or if they are floppy and will not wake up or stay awake [2].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार बहुत आम बात है, और आम तौर पर यह 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, और भूख लगे तो खाना दें [4]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [4]। बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [4]। ध्यान दें: 3 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को भी न दें [2]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाइयों में न लपेटें [2]।

डॉक्टर से मदद लें अगर: 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा हो और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा हो, बुखार के साथ दाने हों, बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहा हो, बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का न लगे और आपको चिंता हो, या निर्जलीकरण के संकेत हों जैसे कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, और रोते समय आँसू न आना [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या स्पंज न करें — NHS के अनुसार बच्चे के कपड़े न उतारें और न ही उसे ठंडा करने के लिए पानी से पोंछें, क्योंकि तेज़ तापमान संक्रमण के प्रति शरीर की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ सकते हैं, सिर्फ़ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य कहता है [3]।

6 महीने के बच्चे का वज़न 5 किलो है, इसलिए उसे इबुप्रोफेन न दें — NHS के अनुसार 3 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को, चिकनपॉक्स या निर्जलीकरण वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन नहीं देना चाहिए [7]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चों को एस्पिरिन भी न दें [7]।

अगर बच्चे को गर्दन में अकड़न, दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने, रोशनी से तकलीफ़, पहली बार दौरा, असामान्य रूप से ठंडे हाथ-पैर, त्वचा या होंठों का रंग नीला-भूरा-पीला पड़ना, नींद में जगाना मुश्किल, बहुत बेचैनी या भ्रम, साँस लेने में तकलीफ़, या सामान्य व्यवहार में बदलाव दिखे तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोंकियल ट्यूबों में रुकावट से होती है, और यह ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं (जैसे साल्बुटामोल) देने पर ठीक हो जाती है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल बीमारियाँ हैं [2]।

अभी बच्चे को आराम से बैठाएँ और शांत रखें, और सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ बढ़ने पर तुरंत मदद लें [2]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई कारणों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे हुए दाने छोटे कीड़ों (स्केबीज़) से हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं; ये अक्सर पहले उंगलियों के बीच दिखते हैं और आमतौर पर घर पर ही इलाज हो सकते हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ में तेज़ खुजली और दाने होते हैं और यह त्वचा से त्वचा के संपर्क से फैलता है [2]।

घर पर खुजली कम करने के लिए: ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, खुजाने के बजाय दानों को थपथपाएँ, और सुगंधित शॉवर जेल या क्रीम न लगाएँ [6]। ढीले सूती कपड़े पहनाएँ और ठंडे पानी से नहाएँ [6]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर: बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों, या घर में किसी और को स्केबीज़ हो; त्वचा में संक्रमण या एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा समस्या हो; कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों; या फार्मेसी का इलाज करने के 2 से 4 हफ्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, फिर भी ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज किया जा सकता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इस बात का संकेत है कि वैक्सीन अपना असर दिखा रही है [6]।

एनआईडायरेक्ट के अनुसार टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम बच्चों को अलग-अलग उम्र में टीके देता है, और एमएमआरवी वैक्सीन की पहली खुराक एक साल की उम्र में दी जाती है [1]। यह उम्र भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार नहीं, बल्कि उस देश के कार्यक्रम के अनुसार है जहाँ यह स्रोत लिखा गया है — भारत में उम्र और खुराक अपने राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं [1]।

टीके समय पर लगवाना ज़रूरी है ताकि सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा मिले, और अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो तो अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करके उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]। टीके सुरक्षित, प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ko khansi aana bachchon mein aam hai, aur yeh asthma ka ek lakshan ho sakta hai: MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [5]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki asthma ke daure mein khansi raat ko ho sakti hai [1].

Ghar par aap kuch cheezein kar sakte hain: bachche ko aaram karne dein, khoob saara taraल दें, saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray dein [4]. Khansi ya zukam ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor se baat karein, kyunki kuch cough aur cold dawaiyon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye recommended nahi hain [4]. Bachchon ko aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein dikkat ho ya saans tez chale, sharir mein paani ki kami ho, bukhar 4 din se zyada rahe, ya lakshan 10 din se zyada behtar na hon [4]. Asthma ke severe attack ke warning signs hain: tez khansi, saans lene mein gambhir dikkat, aur chehre, hothon ya naakhunon ka pale ya neela padna — aise lakshan hon to turant medical help lein [5].
